page: Amazon Web Services t3.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. Memory capacity is provisioned at 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance carries no local NVMe or SSD storage and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, while the baseline network interface is rated at 1 Gbps. It contains no specialized hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Performance profiles for the t3.xlarge are bounded by its burstable CPU allocation model and older microarchitecture. Synthetic benchmarks place its compute throughput in lower performance tiers relative to dedicated compute offerings, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 2125.0 and a single-core score of 946.0. Memory throughput reaches 23.93 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 20.41 GB/sec for large block writes. In application-focused metrics, it sustains 2.65 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.74 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the t3.xlarge offers an economical footprint for workloads requiring a moderate 16 GB memory footprint without sustained, continuous compute demand. The primary tradeoff is the CPU credit mechanism, which limits prolonged peak utilization once burst credits are exhausted. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for low-to-medium traffic web applications, microservices, staging environments, build agents, and lightweight background workers that exhibit intermittent compute activity.
description: Amazon Web Services t3.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz alongside 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The instance features no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results position the server in lower computational tiers, reflecting its shared and burstable CPU credit model with a multi-core Geekbench score of 2125.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3846.12. It provides cost-effective memory density for bursty workloads, making it well suited for non-production environments, intermittent microservices, dev/test setups, and low-traffic web serving.
